- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -1.0 or 0.0) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply a 2–5% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model overreacts; apply 5–10% downward correction to forecast tail.
- When sentiment is uniformly positive and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; add 2–5% lagged momentum adjustment to forecast.
